Synopsis:
The White House has been quietly vetting potential replacements for Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg amid Pentagon leadership turmoil. No removal decision has been made, but the review signals mounting pressure on Feinberg, tied to failures in accelerating munitions production during an ongoing U.S.-Iran war. Senior military and civilian officials — including Army Secretary Driscoll, Navy Secretary Phelan, and other Army leaders — have already departed. Weapons stockpile depletion is a growing strategic concern, with internal blame reportedly directed at Feinberg. Conflict-of-interest questions around his former firm Cerberus and the Golden Dome missile program add further political risk.
